Let me analyze these teaching examples carefully to identify systematic forecast errors and derive correction rules.

Looking at the data patterns:

**Example 1 (2024-10-10):**
- History shows price movement from ~63.21 down to ~60.29, then back up to ~62.01
- The low point was 60.29 on 2024-09-30, then it started recovering
- By 2024-10-10, prices are around 62-65 range
- Model forecasts are generally below true outcomes - the model is too conservative/lower
- True outcomes are notably higher than forecasts across the 30-day horizon
- Looking at sentiment: mostly positive (0.67, 1.00, etc.) with some lows

**Example 2 (2024-10-22):**
- This appears to be a continuation/update of Example 1
- Prices have continued rising - the low point in history is now 61.76 (same as before) but the 30-day ahead outcomes are much higher
- Looking at the first 9 points of the 30d forecast vs outcome comparison:
  - Forecast: [61.95, 64.10, 65.38, 65.21, 64.47, 65.13, 63.35, 62.44, 61.76]
  - Outcome: [62.25, 64.89, 66.63, 66.97, 66.40, 67.28, 65.47, 64.58, 63.87]
- The model is consistently underforecasting by about 0.3-1.0 points in the early part
- But looking further - the outcomes at the end are MUCH higher than forecasts - differences of 2-6 points

**Example 3 (2024-10-11):**
- Very similar to Example 1
- Model forecasts are slightly lower than true outcomes for the first 15 days or so


- The divergence grows in the later days, with outcomes exceeding forecasts by 2-6 points

**Example 4 (2024-10-14):**
- The pattern remains consistent with previous examples
- Model forecasts trail behind true outcomes
- Early differences are around 0.3-1.0 points, expanding to 2-4 points in later observations
